보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: noun

examples.trans: Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 저거 봤어? 앞에서 웃다가 가자마자 표정 싹 바뀌는 거 봤어?
examples.trans: Did you see that? Smiling in front of him and changing her expression completely the second he walked away?
This expression comes from 'smiling and then'.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

examples.text: 너 혜주 좋아하지? 하늘이 무너지는 표정을 짓더라.
examples.trans: You like Hye-joo, right? You looked like the sky was falling earlier.

examples.text: 까나리카노를 마시고 뿜는 표정이 웃겨야 되거든.
examples.trans: Her expression spitting out the fish-sauce coffee has to be hilarious.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 저거 봤어? 앞에서 웃다가 가자마자 표정 싹 바뀌는 거 봤어?
examples.trans: Did you see that? Smiling in front of him and changing her expression completely the second he walked away?
Here the word for 'completely, in a flash' is key.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 바뀌다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (changing).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.trans: She is so two-faced like that!
Here the word for 'like that, so' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: She is so two-faced like that!
Here the word for 'is two-faced!' is key.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 너 너무 예민해, 연예인이라고 24시간 웃고만 있어야 되냐?
examples.trans: You are being way too touchy—just because she is a celebrity, does she have to smile twenty-four hours a day?
This expression comes from 'are touchy, sensitive'.
Did you hear about this celebrity?
I was busy today because of celebrity.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 너 너무 예민해, 연예인이라고 24시간 웃고만 있어야 되냐?
examples.trans: You are being way too touchy—just because she is a celebrity, does she have to smile twenty-four hours a day?
Here the word for 'twenty-four hours' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Are you taking Cindy's side right now?
This expression comes from 'are you taking sides with?'.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 네가 너무 말도 안 되는 트집을 잡으니까.
examples.trans: Because you are picking ridiculous faults for no reason.
Here the word for 'nitpicking fault' is key.
I want to must catch right now.
How about trying to must catch together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.
Did you hear about this idol?
I was busy today because of idol.
Did you hear about this insults, criticism?
I was busy today because of insults, criticism.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너는 남자 아이돌은 욕 안 하잖아, 여자 아이돌만 욕하지.
examples.trans: You never criticize male idols—you only criticize female idols.
This expression comes from 'you badmouth'.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

examples.text: 촬영하고 나면 다음 주 화요일쯤에는 시간 비어.
examples.trans: After filming wraps, I have free time around next Tuesday.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 촬영하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (film and).

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.
Did you hear about this in my heart?
I was busy today because of in my heart.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.
Also means to stamp a seal or dip food into sauce.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
May I take a photo here?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 너한테 짜증 같은 거 한 번도 안 부렸어?
examples.trans: Did she never act cranky toward you even once?
Here the word for 'irritation, crankiness' is key.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너한테 짜증 같은 거 한 번도 안 부렸어?
examples.trans: Did she never act cranky toward you even once?
This expression comes from 'did she vent?'.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
